title: Lunar vs solar tidal split in GNSS receiver clock bias
interpretation: Lunar tides (M2, O1, Q1, J1, N2, M3, M4) detected at all 7 stations.
Grand mean lunar amplitude: 3.368 ns vs solar: 32.463 ns (ratio 0.10).
Mean cross-station phase prediction r: lunar=0.4082, solar=0.2107.
Stack significance: 2/7 lunar, 4/4 solar at p<0.05.
caveats: Only 7 stations available with 45-day contiguous data.
K1 (mixed lunar-solar) excluded from the split to keep it clean.
Ocean loading BLQ coefficients for 6/7 stations are estimated.
Clock-type screening is not significant with 4 quartz vs 2 atomic.
pre_registered_prediction: TEP predicts lunar tides should be detectable and show cross-station phase coherence. Atmospheric origin predicts solar tides should dominate. If lunar phase coherence >= solar phase coherence, the gravitational field interpretation is supported.
